steps.title: Prepare mobile phase solutions
steps.instruction: Make the following solutions in volumes sufficient for the planned number of injections: (a) 85:15 acetonitrile (ACN):H₂O (v/v %) for LC‑method 1 or 1:99 methanol (MeOH):H₂O (v/v %) for LC‑method 2; (b) 10 mM ammonium acetate in H₂O (eluent A) for LC‑method 1 or 0.1 % formic acid in H₂O (eluent A) and 0.1 % formic acid in MeOH (eluent B) for LC‑method 2.

steps.title: Prepare ice‑cold methanol and set temperatures
steps.instruction: Store methanol at –20 °C overnight to obtain ice‑cold MeOH; set the centrifuge and autosampler temperatures to 4 °C.

steps.title: Centrifuge storage tubes
steps.instruction: Centrifuge each saliva‑containing storage tube at 1500 × g for 15 min at 4 °C (the inner holder tube keeps the swab out of the pellet).

steps.title: Remove swabs and aliquot sample
steps.instruction: After centrifugation, remove the swab from each tube. Transfer 25 µL of the recovered liquid to a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube for LC‑method 1 or 40 µL for LC‑method 2 (volume may be adjusted to guarantee material for at least two injections and QC‑pool preparation). Optional: keep extra aliquots as backup.

steps.title: Generate water control samples
steps.instruction: Prepare a minimum of six control samples by adding 30 µL of water to separate 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes and process them in parallel with the study samples.

steps.title: Add ice‑cold methanol (4:1)
steps.instruction: Add ice‑cold methanol to each aliquoted sample in a 4:1 (v/v) methanol‑to‑sample ratio.

steps.title: Incubate at –20 °C
steps.instruction: Place the tubes at –20 °C for 20 min.

steps.title: High‑speed centrifugation and supernatant transfer
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tubes at 18 000 × g for 20 min at 4 °C. Transfer 90 % of the initial supernatant volume into 2 mL glass vials.

steps.title: Dry supernatant
steps.instruction: Dry the transferred supernatant under a gentle stream of nitrogen. (Pause point: store dried samples at –20 °C < 1 week or at –80 °C for longer; limit freeze‑thaw to a single cycle.)

steps.title: Re‑constitute dried extracts
steps.instruction: Re‑dissolve each dried aliquot with 25 µL of 85:15 ACN:H₂O (v/v %) for LC‑method 1 or with 40 µL of 1:99 MeOH:H₂O (v/v %) for LC‑method 2 (same volume as transferred in step 4). Optional: use a smaller volume to concentrate the sample.

steps.title: Sonicate and vortex
steps.instruction: Sonicate the re‑constituted solution for 1 min, then vortex for 5 s.

steps.title: Transfer to analysis vials
steps.instruction: Move the final solution into a glass vial equipped with a micro‑vial insert. Samples are now ready for LC‑MS/MS analysis.

steps.title: Prepare QC pool sample
steps.instruction: Combine an appropriate aliquot from each re‑constituted study sample (excluding control samples) into a single glass vial with a micro‑vial insert to generate a QC‑pool.

steps.title: Prepare blank sample
steps.instruction: Fill a glass vial with 85:15 ACN:H₂O (v/v %) for LC‑method 1 or with 1:99 MeOH:H₂O (v/v %) for LC‑method 2 to serve as a blank; prepare enough blanks for the entire analytical batch.

steps.title: Set up LC‑method 1
steps.instruction: Configure a Nexera X2 UHPLC (or comparable) with an Acquity UPLC BEH HILIC column (130 Å, 1.7 µm, 2.1 × 100 mm) kept at 40 °C. Use an injection volume of 2 µL. Mobile phases: eluent A = 10 mM ammonium acetate in H₂O; eluent B = ACN. Flow rate = 0.4 mL min⁻¹. Gradient: 0–1 min 95 % B, 1–9 min linear to 40 % B, 9–10 min hold at 40 % B, 10.5–17.5 min return to 95 % B for equilibration.

steps.title: Set up LC‑method 2
steps.instruction: Configure a Nexera X2 UHPLC (or comparable) with a Synergi Hydro‑RP column (100 Å, 2.5 µm, 2 × 100 mm) kept at 40 °C. Use an injection volume of 2 µL. Mobile phases: eluent A = 0.1 % formic acid in H₂O; eluent B = 0.1 % formic acid in MeOH. Flow rate = 0.4 mL min⁻¹. Gradient identical to LC‑method 1 (0–1 min 95 % B, 9–10 min 40 % B, 10.5–17.5 min 95 % B).

steps.title: Configure mass spectrometer
steps.instruction: Set the TripleTOF 6600 (or comparable) as follows: Source type = ESI; CUR gas = 30 psi; GAS = 130 psi; GAS = 225 psi; ISVF = 5500 V (−4500 V); TEM = 500 °C; Cycle time = 0.62 s; DP = 80 eV (−80 eV); CE = 10 eV (−10 eV); MS1 scan range = 100–1000 m/z; MS2 scan range = 50–1000 m/z; Accumulation time = 50 ms; IDA mode with intensity > 100 cps; max 20 candidates per cycle; exclude former target ions; mass tolerance = 50 ppm; CE = 30 eV (−30 eV) and 15 eV (−15 eV) for the two CE settings; MS2 start mass = 50 Da, end mass = 1000 Da; MS2 accumulation time = 26 ms; other parameters as listed in Table 2 (including ESI‑ + /‑ mode values in brackets).

steps.title: Run LC‑MS/MS analysis
steps.instruction: Inject each prepared sample, QC‑pool, and blank according to the selected LC method and acquire data with the configured MS parameters.

steps.title: Process data with MS‑DIAL
steps.instruction: Import raw files into MS‑DIAL v4.20 and apply the settings in Table 3: MS1 tolerance = 0.01 Da, MS2 tolerance = 0.025 Da, mass range = 100–1000 Da, max charge = 2, minimum peak width = 8, minimum peak height = 1000, sigma window = 0.5, etc. Use the listed adduct list, retention‑time tolerances, and scoring thresholds. Perform peak alignment, background subtraction using water controls (BgT = mean + 3 × SD of control peak areas, n = 5), retain features present in all replicates, filter by QC‑pool RSD ≤ 20 %, and export the final feature table.
